_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 23 (Sarah's death; purchase of Machpelah). Saadia-specific moves: v.4 'גריב או צ'יף' = 'a stranger or a guest' (Saadia uses 'or' instead of 'and'); v.6 'שריף אללה' = 'noble of God' (substitutes for נשיא אלהים, treating נשיא as 'noble/chief'); v.9 'אלמג'ארה אלמצ'אעפה' = 'the doubled cave' (Saadia treats 'המכפלה' descriptively); v.10 'בני חת' identified as v.3 'sons of Heth' (Canaanite tribe).

translations.1: The lifetime of Sarah was a hundred and twenty-seven years — the years of her life.
translations.2: And Sarah died in Kiriath-Arba — that is Hebron — in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to mourn her and to weep for her.
translations.3: Then Abraham arose from the presence of his dead; and he spoke to the sons of Heth, saying:
translations.4: 'I am a stranger or a guest among you — give me a burial possession with you, that I may bury my dead from before me.'
translations.5: And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him:
translations.6: 'Hear us, O our lord — you are noble of God in our midst; in the choice of our graves bury your dead; and not one man among us shall withhold from you his grave, that you may bury your dead in it.'
translations.7: And Abraham arose, and bowed down in thanks to the dwellers of the land, the sons of Heth.
translations.8: Then he spoke with them, and said to them: 'If your souls desire that I should bury my dead from before me, hear me, and intercede for me with Ephron the son of Zohar,
translations.9: that he may give me the doubled cave (Machpelah) which is his — which is at the edge of his field — for the full price let him give it to me, in your midst, as a burial possession.'
translations.10: And Ephron was sitting among them; and Ephron the Hittite answered in the presence of the sons of Heth and the rest of those who entered the gate of his city, saying:
translations.11: 'No, my lord, hear me — the field I have given to you, and the cave which is in it; in the presence of my kinsmen I have given it to you. Bury your dead in it.'
translations.12: And Abraham bowed down in thanks before the dwellers of the land.
translations.13: Then he spoke with him in their presence, saying: 'But you — yet would that you would hear me — let me give you the price of the field; accept it from me, that I may bury my dead there.'
translations.14: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him:
translations.15: 'My lord, hear me — a field worth four hundred shekels of silver, between me and you — what is it? Bury your dead in it.'
translations.16: And when Abraham heard him in this matter, he weighed out for him the silver which he had named in their presence — four hundred shekels of silver, current in the merchants' trade.
translations.17: And the field of Ephron, known as the doubled, which was over against Mamre — the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees which were in it and in all its border round about —
translations.18: passed to Abraham as a purchase, in the presence of the sons of Heth, and the rest of those who entered the gate of his city.
translations.19: And after that Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the doubled field, over against Mamre — that is Hebron — in the land of Canaan.
translations.20: And the field, and the cave which was in it, was confirmed to Abraham as a burial possession, from the sons of Heth.
